## Review verdict — ✅ accept

Reviewed at `4d99feea` through the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035). Correctness lens, converged. Judge spend $2.2606, 468.7s, one juror, session `6f1b98d9`.

### Round 1 found a real blocker

`buildVerdictComment`'s heading ternary was never extended for the new target, so a re-stamped **acceptance** fell through to the **bounce** arm and would have announced itself as "🔁 review — changes requested". A durable comment that states the opposite of what happened is worse than no comment: the label would say accepted, the prose would say bounced, and a reader believes the prose. Fixed with its own heading — no review was run, so the record must not imply one. Mutation-verified.

Round 1's second finding (the `!reviewHeld` guard being unreachable through `classifyPr`) was addressed by labelling the test as depth against an unreachable state rather than deleting the guard.

### This round's finding, and what chasing it turned up

> `restampAcceptance()` shells `review-set-label.mjs --to=restamp` without pinning `cwd` to the PR's own repo clone, unlike every sibling git-touching call in the same rebase-drop loop.

Carve-out, `worseThanBase: false`. **On its stated terms it is a false positive** — verified rather than assumed: the `gh` calls all take `--repo` explicitly, and the verdict ledger writes to `$HOME/.claude/verdict-ledger` keyed by repo slug from the record. Neither reads `cwd`.

**But the instinct was right, and it found something the stated reason missed.** `review-set-label.mjs` carries this at its fingerprint call:

> NO EXPLICIT `cwd` HERE, AND THAT IS AN INVARIANT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT (PR #1087 review, note 2). This CLI is single-PR and operator-invoked… unlike the drain, which sweeps three repos in one process. **If this CLI ever grows a `--repo` that can name a repo other than the cwd's, this call has to take a `cwd` with it, or it will fingerprint the wrong tree.**

This PR makes **the drain** a caller of that CLI, with an explicit `--repo` that can name a remote constellation repo. That is precisely the condition the invariant names.

It does not fire today: `restamp` is not in the `to === 'accepted' || to === 'clear-human'` list that computes `reviewedDiff`, so no fingerprint is computed and only `reviewed-sha` is stamped. That is sufficient for the loop this PR fixes — the SHA marker matches the new head, which is what the staleness gate's first tier reads — and it fails toward the stricter path, never the looser one.

But it is a **trap I created**: adding `restamp` to that list later, to carry the diff and contribution fingerprints properly, would silently fingerprint the wrong tree in a multi-repo sweep. Filed rather than fixed here, because the fix is a comment and this PR now costs $2.26 and ~8 minutes per review round — it timed out at the 10-minute wall once already.

### On that timeout

Round 2 was killed by `judgeSpawn`'s 600s backstop. #1472's body argued that bound was "a bound on runaway rather than on thoroughness — measured wall times were 167–312s". Those were times **under the $1.5 ceiling** that #1472 removed. Remove one bound and the other becomes binding; this run took 468.7s.
